title: POC scoping — multilingual model shortlist & workload sizing (Lingual Insights)
summary: Initial scoping for a 6-week POC to evaluate open-models for multilingual legal summarization and routing. Discussed success criteria (quality thresholds per language, latency < 500ms 95p on short summaries, throughput targets), shortlist of models to test (mix of 7B-13B open models and quantized variants), workload sizing (peak QPS, avg tokens, KV cache needs), proposed benchmarks and timeline, and next steps including security docs and a small benchmark dataset.
topics: Model shortlist and tradeoffs (7B vs 13B, quantized vs fp16)
Benchmark plan & datasets (legal docs in EN/FR/DE/JA)
Security & deployment constraints (VPC, audit logs, KMS)
next_steps: Redwood to share POC playbook and benchmark template by 2026-09-25
Customer to provide 200 sample documents across languages by 2026-09-28
Schedule technical setup call with Marco and Diego for VPC/network on 2026-09-29
Redwood to propose final model shortlist and suggested quantization profiles by 2026-09-30
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pricing ranges and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison (due 2026-09-25)
Diego Ramos: Prepare benchmark harness and measurement sheet (due 2026-09-27)
Priya Sharma: Upload labeled sample set and success-metric spreadsheet (due 2026-09-28)
Marco Li: Provide network constraints and proxy rules for VPC (due 2026-09-29)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes

[00:00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood Inference team, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Could you each do a 1-minute intro?
[00:00:14] Priya (Lingual Insights): Hi all, I'm Priya, head of ML, we build a multilingual summarization and routing product for law firms, so privacy and accuracy is huge for us.
[00:00:25] Tom (CTO): Tom here, I'm focused on infra and deadlines; we're trying to get a pilot live in Q4.
[00:00:31] Elena (NLP Eng): Elena, I own model evaluation and labeling at Lingual. We'll be doing qual evals and some human-in-the-loop checks.
[00:00:38] Marco (SRE): Marco, SRE, I'll handle network/VPC details.
[00:00:42] Maya: Great. Agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist, benchmarks, timeline, security. Sound good?
[00:00:50] All: Yes.

[00:01:05] Maya: Ok first, success criteria. Priya, what does success look like for the POC?
[00:01:12] Priya: Two big things: 1) Quality — we need extractive/abstractive summaries that meet a minimum human score; our internal rubric uses ROUGE-L and a 1-5 human quality scale. Ideally, average human score >= 4.0 for English, >= 3.8 for French and German, and >= 3.5 for Japanese. 2) Performance — we need latency under 500 milliseconds p95 on short summaries (~200 tokens) and reasonable cost per doc. Also stability with bursts during work day.
[00:01:52] Diego: Quick clarifying q — when you say human score, is that strictly human labeler consensus, or is there a blended automated metric?
[00:02:00] Priya: We'll do blended: human spot-checks plus automated ROUGE/BLEU style. But humans are the tiebreaker.

[00:02:15] Maya: Noted. For the latency target, is p95 500ms an absolute or a stretch?
[00:02:22] Tom: It's a hard requirement for our UI, we can accept higher cost to meet it but not regular spikes above 600ms.

[00:02:30] Diego: Ok. Now workload sizing — Marco, can you describe traffic shape and concurrency?
[00:02:36] Marco: Typical day: 5000 requests/day, peak concurrency about 40 QPS during US morning, average payload ~150 tokens input, output ~180 tokens. But for batch runs (nightly reprocessing) we might do larger volumes — ~50k docs over several hours.
[00:02:59] Elena: Plus some long-context legal briefs — we have edge cases up to 4k tokens where we want chunked summarization.
[00:03:07] Diego: That matters for KV cache and memory. If you have 4k tokens we need to plan model selection and instance sizing. For POC, we usually simulate both short summaries and chunked long-context workflows.

[00:03:22] Maya: Ok model shortlist discussion: given multilingual and cost targets, we propose a mix: smaller 7B-class models for lower cost and faster latency, and 13B-class for quality-critical languages. Initial shortlist we've been thinking: Mixtral-7B (Mistral family), Llama 3 8B variant, Mistral 7B-instruct quantized, and a 13B open model (Llama3-13B or similar) for comparison. Any preferences?
[00:03:56] Priya: We prefer open models, yes. For Japanese we saw better results on 13B in our earlier tests. Also we've heard about Redwoo—s Redwood-verified 13B? (laughs) Sorry, that was mis-specified, but are there Redwood-optimized variants?
[00:04:12] Maya: We maintain performance profiles of models in our catalog; we can surface vetted performance numbers and quantization recommendations. Note there may be transcription errors in the catalog name, but we'll share exact model IDs.
[00:04:22] Tom: Important tradeoff: 7B will hit latency more easily in hosted mode. 13B may need Dedicated or bigger instances to meet p95 targets — cost is a question.
[00:04:32] Diego: Right — typical guidance: 7B quantized to 4-bit on A100-like hardware can give great p95 for short sequences, but for long-context or Japanese nuances we might need 13B fp16 or q4_0 with extra memory. We'll propose candidate quant profiles.

[00:04:50] Elena: For evaluation, we want to include few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought style prompts for complex summarization. That can inflate token counts, so include that in perf runs.
[00:05:00] Diego: Definitely. We'll run both single-turn and multi-turn chain prompts.

[00:05:10] Maya: Benchmarks — our proposed plan: Redwood sends a benchmark harness and template, Lingual supplies 200 labeled examples across EN/FR/DE/JA (50 each). We'll measure quality (ROUGE-L, BLEU, and human score), latency p50/p95, tokens per second, and $/doc. Also include failure rates and model drift indicators.
[00:05:32] Priya: Agreed. Can you support bilingual evaluation? Some docs mix EN/FR in the same file.
[00:05:38] Diego: We can. We'll add specific test cases for code-switch or mixed-language docs. That's important for legal filings in Canada.

[00:05:48] Marco: On infra — we need VPC peering and strict egress policies. Also audit logs retention for 1 year for compliance.
[00:05:57] Maya: We have Private options and Dedicated. For this POC we recommend Hosted for speed to test models quickly, and then Dedicated/VPC for later stages. But if you require VPC from day 1 for data residency, we can spin up a Private control plane — it adds time. How strict is your policy?
[00:06:12] Tom: For pilot we can use Hosted if data is anonymized, but network rules for the SRE team must be respected. We'll provide the allowed IP ranges.

[00:06:22] Diego: Good. Now timelines: We suggest 6 weeks: Week 0-1: dataset + infra prep, Week 2: benchmark runs on 7B candidates, Week 3: 13B runs and qualitative review, Week 4: human eval and cost analysis, Week 5: tuning (prompting/quantization), Week 6: pilot report and recommendation. Does that align with your Q4 pilot goal?
[00:06:44] Priya: Yes, that fits if we can turn around samples quickly.

[00:06:50] Elena: A question on measurement: for human score, do you recommend crowd workers or internal graders?
[00:06:55] Maya: For legal domains we usually recommend internal subject-matter reviewers for final pass because crowd workers won't have the domain expertise. For volume, you can do automated metrics and a smaller internal judge set.

[00:07:06] Diego: Also we'll instrument token-level cost and latency per model so you can see tradeoffs. We may set up canary routing to compare two models in production-like traffic.

[00:07:18] Tom: About canary — we'd want fallback policies to a lower-cost model under capacity pressure. Does Redwood support automatic fallback?
[00:07:24] Maya: Yes, we have routing policies — you can route based on latency, tier, or region, and set automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. We'll show a sample policy.

[00:07:34] Priya: Security: KMS integration is needed for keys. Also we need audit logs with user-level attribution.
[00:07:41] Marco: And ability to rotate keys without downtime.
[00:07:44] Maya: KMS integrations are supported; we have audit logs and can discuss retention. Key rotation can be done with minimal disruption — we'll document the steps.

[00:07:54] Elena: For multilingual quality, will you run few-shot in-language examples or use language-specific fine-tuned variants?
[00:08:00] Diego: Initially few-shot in-language. If we see consistent deficits, we can try small adapter-style fine-tuning or prompt tuning depending on your data policies. Note: training in hosted mode has constraints; for Private you can do more customized fine-tuning.

[00:08:14] Tom: Cost question — how do you present $/doc for mixed model routing?
[00:08:19] Maya: We'll produce a cost simulation showing $/doc across traffic mixes, including routing policies and batching. We'll include quantized model run costs.

[00:08:30] Priya: Benchmarks — we want to look at error modes: hallucination rate, missed jurisdiction references, and named-entity accuracy. Can the benchmark harness capture those?
[00:08:39] Diego: Yes, but you'll need labeled tests for those items. We'll add custom metric hooks so you can plug in your scripts.

[00:08:48] Priya: Good. Also, small nit — in prior tests some transcriptions of model names got mangled so please include exact model identifiers in the sheet.
[00:08:56] Maya: Absolutely. We'll provide model IDs, Docker tags, and quant profiles.

[00:09:05] Marco: Network detail: we need to ensure TLS mutual auth and private IP egress for internal connections. Is mutual TLS supported?
[00:09:12] Diego: We can do mTLS in Private/Dedicated setups. Hosted supports TLS but not necessarily mTLS without Private networking. We'll clarify.

[00:09:22] Tom: One more — what about monitoring? We need token-level breakdowns, per-model latency dashboards, and tracing into our app.
[00:09:30] Maya: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can provide short demo screenshots and dashboard exports.

[00:09:40] Priya: How about evaluation in languages with fewer benchmarks like Japanese — any tips for prompt engineering?
[00:09:46] Diego: Use in-context examples in the same script, and consider model-selection: some open models have stronger Japanese support. We'll do A/B tests and surface examples.

[00:09:56] Elena: For long docs, can you demonstrate streaming summaries so we can show partial results in the UI?
[00:10:02] Maya: Yes, we support streaming responses and partial outputs; we'll include an example integration snippet.

[00:10:10] Tom: Let's talk about failure scenarios — if a 13B node OOMs on a 4k sequence, what's the graceful fallback?
[00:10:17] Diego: We have fallbacks to chunked summarization: the runtime can detect OOM and fall back to chunking or route to a model variant with larger memory. There's an overhead but better than erroring. During POC we'll test those flows.

[00:10:30] Maya: Ok, recap and final alignment — 6-week plan, Redwood provides benchmark harness and model suggestions, Lingual provides 200 samples and SRE constraints, security docs to be exchanged. Next calls: demo of harness on 2026-09-29 and infra deep-dive on 2026-09-29 or 2026-09-30.

[00:10:55] Priya: Sounds good. One last ask: include an embargoed result sharing clause — we don't want benchmark results publicized.
[00:11:02] Maya: Understood; we'll add NDA notes in the POC playbook.

[00:11:10] Tom: Thanks, everyone.
[00:11:12] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings of model names (e.g., "Redwoo" for Redwood), "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cake", filler words present, and some speaker attribution uncertainty around minute 30 where recording dropped briefly.
